quotes: 16 patients representing 7 different pedigrees exhibited an unusual, adult onset limb-girdle myopathy with typical clinical hallmarks. In a majority of cases there was evidence of an autosomal dominant inheritance.

A prominent early finding in all cases was respiratory muscle weakness, and in many of these an acute respiratory incapacity was the reason for the first neurological examination. Neck flexor and sometimes foot extensor weakness were other early symptoms.
Electrophysiological analysis confirmed a myopathy and serum muscle enzyme concentrations were normal or slightly elevated.

quotes: We describe a novel autosomal dominant myopathy presenting in mid-adult life with tibialis anterior weakness. We carried out a detailed clinical assessment of 24 individuals spanning three generations, documenting pathologic features of the muscles in 7 of the 11 affected individuals

Lung function tests revealed progressive global respiratory muscle weakness detectable from the time of presentation, with preferential diaphragmatic involvement in some cases. Hip girdle and shoulder girdle weakness appeared later in the disease course.
The inclusions were Congophilic and reacted with antibodies to desmin, beta-amyloid, and phosphorylated tau protein.

quotes: A combination of genome-wide linkage and whole exome sequencing revealed the likely causal genetic variant in the titin (TTN) gene (g.274375T>C; p.Cys30071Arg) within a shared haplotype of 2.93 Mbp on chromosome 2.

This segregated with the phenotype in 21 individuals from the original family, nine subjects in a second family with the same highly selective pattern of muscle involvement on magnetic resonance imaging and a third familial case with a similar phenotype.

Magnetic resonance muscle imaging was performed in 21 affected patients and revealed characteristic abnormalities with semitendinosus involvement in 20 of 21 patients studied, including 3 patients who were presymptomatic.

notes.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2014) screened 127 undiagnosed UK probands with features compatible with myofibrillar myopathy (MFM) for the TTN p.C30071R and p.R32450W mutations and found heterozygous p.C30071R in 5 (3.9%), including 4 of 72 with a clinical diagnosis of MFM (5.5%); no patient had a mutation at p.32450. Two further patients carried novel heterozygous variants in the 119th FN3 domain (p.P30091L and p.N30145K) of uncertain pathogenicity.
quotes: Sequencing identified the heterozygous g.274375T>C mutation (p.C30071R) in 5/127 unrelated subjects (F.1A, F.2A, F3, F.4B and F.5) with a total detection rate of 3.9% in the entire cohort.
Four of these patients had a clinical diagnosis of MFM, giving a detection rate within this group of 5.5%.
Sequencing for the TTN kinase domain mutation revealed wild-type sequence in all subjects.

notes.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2014) found that probands from 5 new families and 3 previously reported families with TTN p.C30071R shared a common haplotype with a core region of 171 kbp; the probability of this sharing in unrelated families by chance was less than 10(-6), suggesting a British founder effect and an ancient mutation.
quotes: Haplotype analysis indicated a shared region of 171 kbp between all 8 families with the p.C30071R mutation ( and current report), and that the probability of this shared haplotype occurring in 8 unrelated families by chance is less than 10-6.
The very small size of the shared haplotype suggests an ancient mutation, or that (less likely) the mutation occurred more than once in time on similar haplotype backgrounds of approximately 171 kbp.

notes.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2014) described onset in the fourth or fifth decade with tripping, falling, myalgia and walking difficulty, slow progression involving proximal, distal and axial muscles, and CK up to 1195 IU/L. Ten of 11 patients had respiratory muscle weakness on pulmonary function testing, with nocturnal noninvasive ventilation required 20 to 30 years after onset in 4; newly noted features included often asymmetric scapular winging, elbow and Achilles tendon contractures, and variable spinal rigidity.
quotes: Onset was typically in the 4th or 5th decades, and symptoms included tripping and falling, myalgia and walking difficulties.

Ten of 11 patients had abnormal pulmonary function tests indicative of respiratory muscle weakness, and requirement for nocturnal noninvasive ventilation occurred approximately 20-30 years after disease onset in 4 patients.
Previously undocumented examination findings in this condition included scapular winging, often asymmetrical, elbow and/or achilles tendon (TA) contractures and a variable degree of spinal rigidity.

notes.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2014) found that muscle MRI showed early involvement of the semitendinosus and peroneus longus muscles. Muscle biopsies showed myopathic or dystrophic changes, rimmed vacuoles, eosinophilic and dark-blue Gomori trichrome inclusions, and accumulation of desmin, myotilin, p62 and ubiquitin in 6 of 7 biopsies, with characteristic 'cheetah skin' myotilin aggregates in 3.
quotes: Findings were consistent with previous reports, with early involvement of the semitendinosus and peroneus longus muscles.
Variable degrees of cytoplasmic accumulation of desmin, myotilin, P62 and ubiquitin was present in 6/7 biopsies.
In three biopsies (F.1B, F.4A and F.5), cytoplasmic aggregates showed a “cheetah skin appearance”, particularly with myotilin staining (Figure 4).

notes.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2014) concluded that TTN mutations are a cause of myofibrillar myopathy and proposed that hereditary myopathy with early respiratory failure (HMERF) due to TTN mutations be classified as MFM-titinopathy.
quotes: We suggest that HMERF due to mutations in the TTN gene be nosologically classified as MFM-titinopathy.

notes.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2014) noted that MFM-titinopathy did not appear to be associated with major cardiac involvement but recommended cardiac surveillance for all patients with TTN mutations, and recommended sequencing of this TTN FN3 domain in the diagnostic workup of MFM, particularly with early respiratory involvement and supportive muscle MRI.
quotes: MFM-titinopathy does not appear to be associated with major cardiac involvement, but in view of titin’s role in myocardial function we recommend cardiac surveillance for all patients with TTN mutations.
sequencing of this FN3 domain of TTN should be performed as part of the diagnostic workup for MFM, particularly in the presence of early respiratory involvement and supportive muscle MRI.

notes.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2014) cautioned that TTN is highly polymorphic: exome data from 239 subjects identified 71 novel TTN coding changes of uncertain significance, apparently randomly distributed across the gene, none in the 119th FN3 domain.
quotes: Exome data from 239 subjects at our centre discovered 71 novel TTN coding changes of uncertain significance.
None of these variants appeared in the 119th FN3 domain (amino acid positions 30068-30160), although these data still indicate that novel coding variants in TTN should be interpreted with caution.

notes.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2012) used genome-wide linkage combined with whole exome sequencing and identified a shared haplotype of 2.93 Mbp on chromosome 2 containing the likely causal TTN variant.
quotes: A combination of genome-wide linkage and whole exome sequencing revealed the likely causal genetic variant in the titin (TTN) gene (g.274375T>C; p.Cys30071Arg) within a shared haplotype of 2.93 Mbp on chromosome 2.

notes.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2012) found that the disorder presented with predominant distal, proximal, or respiratory muscle weakness, with highly variable onset from early adulthood, including a mild phenotype in advanced age; weakness was earlier and more severe in the lower extremities, respiratory function deteriorated progressively, and no patient developed cardiomyopathy over up to 31 years of follow-up.
quotes: The clinical presentation included predominant distal, proximal or respiratory muscle weakness. The age of onset was highly variable, from early adulthood, and including a mild phenotype in advanced age.
Cardiomyopathy was not present in any of our patients despite up to 31 years of follow-up.

notes.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2012) concluded that the disease should be considered in adult-onset proximal or distal myopathy with early respiratory failure even with nonspecific muscle pathology, that muscle MRI findings are characteristic and should be an initial investigation prompting TTN screening, and that whole exome sequencing offers a reliable cost-effective approach for screening the 363-exon TTN gene if adequately captured.
quotes: This disease should be considered in patients with adult-onset proximal or distal myopathy and early respiratory failure, even in the presence of non-specific muscle pathology.
Muscle magnetic resonance imaging findings are characteristic and should be considered as an initial investigation, and if positive should prompt screening for mutations in TTN.
However, whole exome sequencing provides a reliable cost-effective approach, providing the gene of interest is adequately captured.

notes.statement: Birchall et al. (2005) found that muscle MRI showed selective early involvement of the semitendinosus and obturator externus that could not be detected clinically, with different rates of progression in closely related muscles. They proposed that these findings were specific to the disorder and allowed early noninvasive diagnosis in at-risk individuals.
quotes: These findings are specific to autosomal dominant myopathy with early respiratory failure and enable early non-invasive diagnosis for individuals at risk.

notes.statement: Birchall et al. (2005) described the disorder as a dominant limb myopathy with early respiratory failure while patients could still walk. Onset was insidious in late adult life, and muscle involvement was highly selective both clinically and pathologically.
quotes: We recently described a dominant limb myopathy characterised by early respiratory failure whilst affected individuals were still ambulant
because of the insidious onset in late adult life and the highly selective muscle involvement, both clinically and pathologically

notes.statement: Lange et al. (2005) reported that a human mutation in the protein kinase domain of titin causes hereditary muscle disease by disrupting a mechanically regulated signaling pathway involving nbr1, p62/SQSTM1, and MuRF2.
quotes: A human mutation in the titin protein kinase domain causes hereditary muscle disease by disrupting this pathway.

notes.statement: Lange et al. (2005) identified a signaling complex in which the titin kinase domain interacts with the zinc-finger protein nbr1 through a mechanically inducible conformation. Nbr1 targets the ubiquitin-associated protein p62/SQSTM1 to sarcomeres, and p62 in turn interacts with MuRF2, a muscle-specific E3 ligase that binds the transactivation domain of SRF.
quotes: We identified a signaling complex where TK interacts with the zinc-finger protein nbr1 through a mechanically inducible conformation.

Nbr1 targets the ubiquitin-associated p62/SQSTM1 to sarcomeres, and p62 in turn interacts with MuRF2, a muscle-specific RING-B-box E3 ligase and ligand of the transactivation domain of the serum response transcription factor (SRF).

notes.statement: Lange et al. (2005) found that mechanical inactivity induced nuclear translocation of MuRF2. This reduced nuclear SRF and repressed transcription, which links titin kinase mechanosensing to the control of muscle gene expression and protein turnover.
quotes: Nuclear translocation of MuRF2 was induced by mechanical inactivity and caused reduction of nuclear SRF and repression of transcription.

notes.statement: Chinnery et al. (2001) excluded linkage of the disorder in this family to all known loci associated with distal myopathies, concluding that the disorder was genetically and phenotypically distinct.
quotes: The disease was not linked to any of the known loci associated with distal myopathies, confirming that the disorder in this family is both genetically and phenotypically distinct.

notes.statement: Chinnery et al. (2001) observed a striking correlation between clinical and pathologic features: clinically unaffected muscles showed minimal change, moderately affected muscles showed fiber splitting, eosinophilic inclusions and rimmed vacuoles, and severely involved muscles were replaced by fat and fibrous connective tissue.
quotes: We observed a striking correlation between the clinical and pathological features. Clinically unaffected muscles had minimal pathologic change.

Fiber splitting, eosinophilic inclusions, and vacuoles with basophilic rims were seen in moderately affected muscles, and fat and fibrous connective tissue replaced muscle fibers in the severely involved muscles.

notes.statement: In a French family with a clinical phenotype and muscle biopsy findings similar to those of the Swedish families with autosomal dominant myopathy with proximal weakness and early respiratory muscle involvement mapped to 2q24-q31, Xiang et al. (1999) completely excluded linkage to the 2q24-q31 region.
quotes: a French family with a similar clinical phenotype and pathology (muscle biopsy) was investigated to see whether the disease gene associated with the myopathy is mapped to the same region as the one in the Swedish families; however, chromosomal region 2q24-q31 was completely excluded.

notes.statement: Xiang et al. (1999) ran a genome-wide scan in the French family and found a maximum 2-point lod score of 2.11 for markers in a 4-cM region between D2S1272 and D2S1260. This was the highest lod score the family could achieve. They concluded that the gene responsible for the French form was likely located on chromosome 2q21.
quotes: A maximum two-point lod score of 2.11 (the highest lod score that can be achieved in this family) was obtained for the markers in the region between D2S1272 and D2S1260, spanning 4 cM.
This result suggests that the gene responsible for the French form is likely to be located on chromosome 2q21.

notes.statement: In 2 Swedish families with autosomal dominant myopathy with proximal weakness and early respiratory failure, Nicolao et al. (1999) performed a genomewide linkage screen and established linkage to chromosome 2q24-q31, with a maximum combined 2-point lod score of 4.87 at theta = 0 for marker D2S1245. Haplotype analysis placed the gene within a 17-cM region between markers D2S2384 and D2S364.
quotes: Linkage to the chromosomal region 2q24-q31 was established. A maximum combined two-point LOD score of 4.87 at a recombination fraction of 0 was obtained with marker D2S1245.
Haplotype analysis indicated that the gene responsible for the disease is likely to be located in the 17-cM region between markers D2S2384 and D2S364.

notes.statement: Nicolao et al. (1999) found that affected individuals from the 2 Swedish families shared an identical haplotype, suggesting a common origin (founder effect).
quotes: The affected individuals from these two families share an identical haplotype, which suggests a common origin.

notes.statement: Edström et al. (1990) found that muscle biopsies contained myofibrillar plaques that stained strongly with rhodamine-conjugated phalloidin, an F-actin marker. On electron microscopy, the plaques were made of moderately dense thin filaments and were related to Z-disc splitting or extended from Z-discs.
quotes: Muscle biopsy findings revealed myofibrillar changes which, at the light microscopy level, included plaques that stained strongly with rhodamine-conjugated phalloidin, a specific marker for F-actin.
At the ultrastructural level, these plaques were observed to be composed of moderately dense, thin filaments and were related to splitting of Z-discs or formed extensions from Z-discs.

notes.statement: Edström et al. (1990) suggested that the biopsy changes pointed to defective myofibrillogenesis. They raised the possibility of defective actin polymerization.
quotes: We believe that the muscle biopsy changes revealed by cytochemical and ultrastructural observations indicate defective myofibrillogenesis, and the possibility of defective actin polymerization is discussed.

notes.statement: Edström et al. (1990) found evidence of autosomal dominant inheritance in most of the 7 pedigrees.
quotes: In a majority of cases there was evidence of an autosomal dominant inheritance.
